findings.title: The new root Node suite is still missing from ci.yml, so the always-on CI enumeration guard fails at this head
findings.detail: Still unfixed at 2ef65d09e. The only change since round 2 is engineering/doc/FLY-2391-auto-release-veto/progress.md. The code diff against the merge base for packages/ and scripts/ is byte-identical to 8ae78c798 (same sha256 of `git diff 579c79ed..HEAD -- packages scripts`), and .github/workflows/ci.yml is untouched. scripts/__tests__/ci-shell-suite-enumeration.test.sh (FLY-1764/FLY-2388) requires every `scripts/__tests__/*.test.mjs` to appear literally in ci.yml. Reproduced at this head: `grep -c customer-release-reservation .github/workflows/ci.yml` gives 0, and the guard exits 1 with `[FAIL] Node suites missing from ci.yml: - scripts/__tests__/customer-release-reservation.test.mjs`. That guard runs in the always-on lane (ci.yml step 'Verify shell suite CI enumeration is complete'), so required CI cannot go green, and the concurrency proof it adds would never run in CI. progress.md says further commits (8f60020c6, 73b61f44c) sit on a detached /tmp branch to be cherry-picked later; they are not part of the reviewed head and do not change this. Fix: add `node --test scripts/__tests__/customer-release-reservation.test.mjs` to the 'Test — root Node contract suites' run block (ci.yml:132-146). The fixture scripts/__tests__/fixtures/customer-release-reserve-worker.mjs is not matched by the guard and needs no wiring.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR opened at 2ef65d09e runs the always-on 'Verify shell suite CI enumeration is complete' step. ci-shell-suite-enumeration.test.sh exits 1 because customer-release-reservation.test.mjs is not listed in ci.yml. Required CI is red on the exact head, so the change cannot land, and force-landing it would break the governance lane for every branch.

findings.title: invalidate() appends a new post_claim_intervention event on every call, even when the cycle is already latched (unbounded growth)
findings.detail: Carried over, unchanged at this head. For cycles in committing, commit_unknown or published, invalidate() never checks whether the cycle is already latched. It always inserts a post_claim_intervention event and bumps revision, while invalidated_event_seq only sticks via COALESCE. invalidateSourceMatch() reads each matched row's current revision before calling it, so the revision guard never stops a repeat. Re-verified at this head: 25 identical invalidateSource(sha,'heartbeat_unhealthy') calls on a published cycle wrote 25 post_claim_intervention events and left revision=25, while invalidatedEventSeq stayed 2. The callers fire repeatedly: appendReleaseHeartbeat on every unhealthy patrol tick, appendReleaseReadinessVerdict on every non-green verdict (rider tick, /report/render, GET /verdict), and recordReleaseFounderScan on every rider tick while a 👎 stays on the report. A published cycle's decision fullBinding.sourceCommit is the deployed sha, so it keeps matching while that build stays deployed. customer_release_events is registered as protectedAuthority and is never pruned, so rows grow without limit in the Bridge's primary SQLite DB, and the post_claim_intervention metric in plan.md §12 stops meaning anything. Nothing reaches this today (no runtime, flag off by default), but fix it before the runtime lands: skip the event and revision bump when the cycle is already latched with the same reason, or dedupe on (cycle_id, kind, reason).
findings.failure_scenario: Cycle C for project flywheel is published on commit S, and S stays deployed. The founder leaves a 👎 on the readiness report. Each patrol tick then calls recordReleaseFounderScan(sentiment:'down'), which calls invalidateSource(S,'founder_down'). Every tick appends another post_claim_intervention row for C and bumps C.revision, with no end, in a table that retention never deletes.

findings.title: A late no_write result can move a cycle out of commit_unknown back to awaiting_attempt, releasing the lock-out the plan requires
findings.detail: Carried over, unchanged at this head. The replay guard is `prior && (prior.kind !== 'unknown' || result.kind === 'unknown')`. When prior.kind is 'unknown' and result.kind is 'no_write', the guard is false and execution continues. commit_unknown passes the committing/commit_unknown state check, and the no_write branch sets the cycle back to awaiting_attempt, which lets claimAuto run again. plan.md T14/T16 and §8.3 step 6 say commit_unknown may only be resolved by exact committed evidence (T15) or a won abandon CAS (T16). validateAttemptResult asks for no manifest evidence on no_write, only reason in {guard_rejected, cas_conflict}. The damage is limited: a re-claim re-derives the binding from the live manifest (the op must still be prepared), and the endpoint CAS is bound to the ETag, so a real double commit still cannot land. But the lock-out is weaker than the plan says, and no test covers it: T14 only replays `unknown`. Fix: reject no_write when the attempt's recorded prior kind is 'unknown'.
findings.failure_scenario: Attempt A1's PUT times out, and the cycle latches commit_unknown. Later a reconciler or a buggy adapter reports {kind:'no_write', reason:'guard_rejected'} for the same attempt identity. recordAttemptResult returns 'awaiting_attempt', and claimAuto can mint a second permit while A1's outcome is still genuinely unknown.

findings.title: Readiness probe routes open to the scoped token can permanently cancel the week's release cycle
findings.detail: Carried over, unchanged at this head. appendReleaseReadinessVerdict now calls customerReleases.invalidateSource(subject.sourceCommit, ...) for any non-green verdict, and that cancellation latch is permanent. GET /api/release-readiness/verdict (routes.ts:119) and POST /report/render both reach this write. GET /verdict takes the subject from the query string, checked for format only. Both routes sit behind tokenAuthMiddleware(apiToken, geminiAgentToken), so the scoped agent token is enough. In evaluate.ts, a baseVersion that differs from the versions seen in heartbeats adds a subject_mismatch reason, and any reason makes the state non-green. Anyone holding the scoped token who knows the deployed sha can therefore cancel that week's cycle for good. This fails closed: it can only block a publish, never cause one, because the claim path requires the verdictId produced by its own in-transaction evaluate(). Still, the plan means the latch to come from the scheduler's own evaluation. Limit the invalidation to scheduler-originated evaluations, or require subject === deps.subject() on these routes.
findings.failure_scenario: A runner holding the scoped token calls GET /verdict?commit=<deployed sha>&baseVersion=<a validly formatted but different version>. The evaluation adds subject_mismatch, the persisted verdict is 'unknown', invalidateSource cancels the live cycle, and the latch keeps it cancelled even after readiness turns green again.

findings.title: The cross-process reservation test cannot guarantee the two children actually contend for the write lock
findings.detail: Carried over, unchanged at this head. The worker sends 'attempting' and only afterwards calls store.reserve(), which runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The parent COMMITs as soon as both messages arrive, and nothing forces the children's BEGIN IMMEDIATE to happen before that COMMIT. If the parent wins the race, the two reserves just run one after the other and the test still passes. Its assertions are correct (one row, one cycle_reserved event, identical returned cycles), but it can go green without ever exercising the contended path that implementation.md cites it as proving. Fix: have the worker signal from inside a busy handler, or assert that at least one child actually waited on the lock.
findings.failure_scenario: On a loaded CI runner, the parent handles both 'attempting' messages and COMMITs before either child starts its transaction. The reserves then run one after the other against an unlocked database, and the test passes without testing contention.

findings.title: manual.go() accepts delivery evidence supplied with the action instead of a receipt persisted earlier
findings.detail: Carried over, unchanged at this head. In the auto path, the delivery receipt is stored before the veto window opens, and later checks compare against that stored row. The manual path has no such earlier record. go() receives `delivery` in the same call as the founder's action, compares it only to the card fields and the action's messageId, and writes delivery_json for the first time in that same statement. The adapter therefore vouches for both the click and the proof of delivery. Nothing reaches this yet, since no Gateway is wired. When the adapter lands, store a manual delivery receipt when the card is sent and have go() match against it.
findings.failure_scenario: A future adapter with a buggy message read-back builds the delivery object from the card itself. go() accepts it and moves the cycle to manual_ready without any independently stored proof that the card was delivered.

findings.title: cancel_reason stays set when a cycle moves from cancelled to manual_ready to committing
findings.detail: Carried over, unchanged at this head. Neither go() nor manual.claim() clears cancel_reason, so a cycle that is committing or published under a founder go still carries its original auto-cancellation reason until the first attempt result overwrites it. Readers that show state next to cancel_reason will display a contradiction. This affects reporting only.
findings.failure_scenario: A summary shows state='committing' next to cancelReason='readiness_hold', which suggests the cycle was stopped while it is actually publishing.
